A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMCL/DNS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-J support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F report original classification/retrieval experiments, stability and plasticity analyses, learning curves, and computational timing.

after.justification: Retains the original empirical results and adds modality-imbalance, misalignment, and noise experiments in Appendix F, Tables 4-6.

M1.justification: The dual-sided gradient projection, feature-covariance updates, pretrained backbones, linear learners, and training/inference algorithms are retained. The new experiments evaluate the existing DNS method.

E1.justification: The seven named datasets, modalities, and classification/retrieval tasks remain unchanged. Appendix F.3-F.5 extends coverage to imbalanced modality exposure, mismatched modality pairs, and Gaussian-corrupted training data.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Vanilla, GEM, DER, DER++, EWC, Co2L, C-FLAT, and CILA. The added robustness comparisons reuse Vanilla and CILA; no new comparison algorithm or revised baseline adaptation is introduced.

E3.justification: New robustness protocols include a four-step text-video/text-audio sequence, feature-swapping ratios, and Gaussian-noise scales at seven levels from 0.01 to 0.5. The original benchmark splits, metrics, training budgets, and hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F.3-F.5 adds a substantive robustness suite examining unequal modality exposure, incorrect pairing, and noisy training data. These questions were not tested in v2, whose existing sensitivity, training-trajectory, stability/plasticity, and efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 still reports means and standard deviations over ten independent trials, with the same trial information in Appendix A.5. New Tables 4-6 report point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or separately specified repeat counts.

E6.justification: Tables 4-6 add substantial comparative results across three robustness scenarios; all 162 mean/standard-deviation entries in Table 2 and the original plots are unchanged. At noise scale 0.5, DNS accuracy is 37.31 versus CILA's 28.52. DNS does not dominate every new metric: at misalignment 0.2, retrieval BWT is -1.85 versus CILA's -1.49. These are newly evaluated conditions, not improvements over corresponding v2 results.

T1.justification: The stability/plasticity definitions, projection derivations, theoretical bounds, assumptions, and proofs and technical lemmas in Appendices B-C are retained. Reformatting does not alter their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: formulating CMCL, deriving DNS, providing stability/plasticity guarantees, and demonstrating effectiveness across seven datasets. The new robustness evidence supports rather than redefines these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F.3-F.5 newly links greater modality overlap to forgetting and interprets the added comparisons as evidence of robustness. F.4 does not qualify the retrieval-BWT exceptions in Table 5. The existing downstream-generalization limitation and proposed scientific applications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the supplemental-material/future-release statement with a specific code-repository address and an availability claim, although Appendix H still promises future release. The new experiments document their imbalance sequence and perturbation levels; existing implementation and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added: Principled Multimodal Representation Learning, AlphaEdit, LLM2Rec, Both Matter, and SAPT. The related-work narrative and the positioning of CMCL relative to prior research otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. Changes include acknowledgements, publication-header edits, limited copyediting, and organizing Appendix F into named subsections, including headings for previously existing analyses.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS format changes typography, text width, spacing, and figure/table placement throughout the document. Existing graphics are retained but resized or relocated, including Figure 3 and the main results table. Three new robustness tables are added, and Figure 3's caption corrects duplicated modality labels.

improvement.justification: Tables 4-6 usefully extend v2's evidence to imperfect multimodal data, and the abstract supplies a concrete code location. The gains are limited by sparse details and absent uncertainty reporting for the new tests, while F.4's superiority interpretation overlooks retrieval-BWT exceptions. The core method, theory, and original results remain unchanged.
